_comment: Shared fixture for TIME-OF-DAY SLOT assignment — the mood layer's four buckets.
Sibling of schedule-test-vectors.json and it exists for the same reason: the same
logic is implemented twice (TypeScript in web/src/lib/design/slots.ts, Kotlin in the
alarm core when it tints its ground by dose time), and two implementations of one
rule drift. calculateNextReminder already proved that — its two JS copies were
described as 'lockstep' and had silently diverged on empty input.
Share the TESTS, not the code. Both engines must pass every vector below.
Two decisions encoded here, both deliberate:
1. MORNING STARTS AT HOUR 0, not 05:00. A 03:00 dose is real in this app
a small labelling inaccuracy; a dose landing in NO slot and vanishing off the
rail would be a bug. Correctness over label aesthetics.
2. SLOTTING USES THE MEDICATION'S TIMEZONE, never the device's. A dose set for
08:00 Asia/Kolkata is a morning dose even when the phone is in London.
Getting this wrong mistints a travelling patient's entire day.
night [21:00-23:59]. Boundaries are INCLUSIVE at the start of each slot.
expectedSlot is one of: morning | midday | evening | night.

vectors.name: medication timezone wins: same instant is morning in Kolkata
medication timezone wins: same instant is evening in Los Angeles
medication timezone wins: same instant is midday in London
legacy Asia/Calcutta alias matches Asia/Kolkata (both live in real data)
DST: New York spring-forward day, 20:00 local is still evening
DST: New York fall-back day, 08:00 local is morning
null timezone falls back without throwing
unknown timezone must not throw; slot is engine-local
